name: Obsidian Everywhere
tagline: Your Obsidian graph and local semantic context, anywhere
description: Local-first MCP turns your Obsidian vault into graph and semantic context—even for agents on another machine. Search by meaning, build context, and start remote access read-only. Guarded edits and Mount Guard protect writes without hosting the vault.
firstComment:
Hey Product Hunt — I built Obsidian Everywhere after trying to use an AI agent on a remote machine with a vault on my own drive. Existing approaches often meant syncing the whole vault elsewhere or reducing it to plain file search. I wanted the agent to understand both meaning and links while the vault stayed under my control.

v0.7.0 has two core jobs:

- build compact context from local semantic search and the Obsidian link graph
- make that context available to Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT, or any Streamable HTTP MCP client—even on another machine

The safety model matters as much as retrieval:

- start remote setup read-only
- enable guarded writes only when needed
- use targeted edits, dry-run-first bulk tools, snapshots, and rollback
- let Mount Guard block writes if a removable drive, NAS share, or container mount disappears

Obsidian Everywhere needs no hosted account, embedding API key, or telemetry. The embedding model runs locally after its first download. An authenticated MCP request returns only the context requested by the tool.

Watch the complete 44-second workflow:
https://github.com/junnnnnw00/obsidian-everywhere#watch-the-remote-vault-bridge-in-44-seconds

Or try the sample vault without touching your notes:

`npx -y obsidian-everywhere demo`

This is an MIT-licensed one-person FOSS project. I would especially value feedback from people using remote development servers, removable drives, NAS shares, or container mounts: where did setup feel unclear, and which safety check would earn your trust?
